course: Cosmetics: Lip Balms, Body Butters & Hair Oils

lessons.title: Selling to Local Shops and Salons
lessons.body: Start by identifying 10 small shops and salons within a 5 km radius of your production site. Walk in during off-peak hours (mid-morning or early afternoon) and ask to speak to the owner. Bring samples: 3 lip balms, 3 body butters, and 3 hair oils. Offer a free full-size product for the owner to try. If they like it, propose a consignment arrangement: you leave 10 units of each product, they pay you after selling. Set a clear price: your wholesale price should be 60% of your retail price. For example, if you retail a lip balm at KES 300, wholesale is KES 180. The shop sells at KES 300 and keeps KES 120. For salons, offer a bulk deal: 20 hair oils for the price of 15. Provide a simple invoice book (cost: KES 100) and record every transaction. Visit each shop weekly to check stock and collect payments. After one month, if a shop sells well (more than 50% of stock), offer them a 5% discount on their next order. If a shop sells nothing, take back the stock and try another. Use WhatsApp to send reminders and confirm orders. Keep a notebook with each shop's name, contact, products taken, and payment status. This system builds trust and repeat business.

lessons.title: Packaging for Shipping within Africa
lessons.body: Your products must survive rough handling by buses, boda bodas, and postal services. For lip balms, wrap each tube in a small piece of bubble wrap (or newspaper) and place in a zip-lock bag. For body butters, use a strong plastic jar with a screw lid; wrap the jar in a plastic bag, then bubble wrap, then place in a padded envelope or small cardboard box. For hair oils, use a glass or PET bottle; wrap in bubble wrap and seal in a plastic bag to prevent leakage. Use a double-walled cardboard box for multiple items. Fill empty spaces with shredded paper or old newspaper. Seal with strong packing tape (not cello tape). Label the box with the recipient's name, phone number, and address in waterproof marker. Include a small card with your contact and a thank-you note. For shipping within your country, use local bus companies (e.g., in Kenya, Easy Coach or Guardian) â they charge KES 200-500 for a small box up to 5 kg. For cross-border (e.g., Uganda to Kenya), use bus parcel services or courier companies like G4S or DHL, but expect KES 1,500-3,000 for 5 kg. Always get a tracking number or receipt. Test your packaging: drop a packed box from waist height; if it survives, it's good. Buy packaging materials in bulk from local suppliers to save money.

lessons.title: Using Boda Boda and Local Couriers
lessons.body: Boda boda (motorcycle taxis) are the fastest and cheapest way to deliver within a city or town. For a 5 km delivery, expect to pay KES 150-250. For 10 km, KES 300-400. Negotiate the price before the rider leaves. Use a delivery app like Uber Boda (in Kenya), SafeBoda (Uganda), or Bolt (various countries) to book and track. If you use a regular rider, build a relationship: agree on a fixed rate for regular deliveries and give them a small tip during peak seasons. Always package your products securely (see previous lesson) and label clearly. For multiple deliveries in one area, combine them into one trip to save money. For local couriers, consider using Pickup Mtaani (Kenya) or similar agent networks: they charge KES 100-200 per parcel and have pickup points. You drop off the parcel, they deliver to their agent near the customer, and the customer picks it up. This is cheaper but slower (1-2 days). For same-day delivery, use boda boda. Always get a proof of delivery: a photo of the parcel at the customer's door, or a signed slip. Keep a log of all deliveries: date, rider name, destination, cost, and delivery status. If a rider loses or damages a parcel, stop using them. Consider hiring a part-time rider if you have more than 10 deliveries per day.

lessons.title: Managing Inventory and Stock Levels
lessons.body: Keep a simple inventory system: a notebook or a free app like Google Sheets. List each product (e.g., 'Lip Balm - Mint', 'Body Butter - Shea', 'Hair Oil - Coconut') and track: quantity produced, quantity sold, quantity in stock, and reorder level. For each product, set a reorder level: when stock drops to that number, produce more. For fast-moving items (e.g., lip balms), reorder when you have 20 left. For slow movers (e.g., hair oils), reorder when you have 10 left. Count your stock physically every week. Compare with your records. If there's a mismatch, investigate: theft, spoilage, or recording error. Store products in a cool, dark place away from direct sunlight. Use shelves or plastic crates. Keep raw materials (shea butter, oils, beeswax) in sealed containers. Label everything with production date and expiry date (typically 12 months for balms, 6 months for butters, 12 months for oils). Use the FIFO method: First In, First Out. Sell older stock first. If you produce in batches, record batch numbers. This helps if a customer complains. For online orders, keep a separate 'reserved' stock so you don't oversell. Review your inventory weekly and adjust production based on sales trends. During rainy season, sales may drop; produce less. During holidays, produce more.

lessons.title: Handling Returns and Refunds
lessons.body: Have a clear return policy: accept returns within 7 days of purchase if the product is unopened and in original packaging. For opened products, only accept returns if there is a quality issue (e.g., rancid smell, separation, or skin reaction). In that case, offer a replacement or full refund. Never argue with a customer. If a customer complains, listen, apologize, and solve the problem quickly. For local shop returns, visit the shop within 48 hours, inspect the product, and either replace it or credit the shop. For online orders, ask the customer to send a photo of the problem. If valid, send a replacement via boda boda or courier, and ask them to return the defective item if possible. Keep a returns log: date, customer name, product, reason, action taken. Analyze returns monthly. If a specific product has many returns, check your production process: maybe your oil ratio is wrong, or your packaging is leaking. Fix the root cause. For refunds, use mobile money (M-Pesa, MTN MoMo) for speed. Refund within 3 days. If you sold through a shop, refund the shop and let them refund the customer. Always follow up with the customer after a return to ensure they are satisfied. A well-handled return can turn a dissatisfied customer into a loyal one.

lessons.title: Expanding to Online Marketplaces
lessons.body: Start with social media: create a business Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok account. Post photos of your products, show how they are made, and share customer testimonials. Use WhatsApp Business to catalog products and take orders. For wider reach, join local online marketplaces: in Kenya, use Jumia, Kilimall, or Sky.Garden; in Nigeria, Jumia and Konga; in South Africa, Takealot. To sell on Jumia, register as a seller, provide your ID, business permit, and bank details. They charge a commission (typically 10-15%) and a monthly fee. You ship your products to their warehouse or use their drop-ship service. For drop-ship, you keep stock and ship when an order comes. Pack securely and include an invoice. For international marketplaces like Etsy or Amazon, you need a payment gateway (PayPal or Payoneer) and international shipping. Start with local marketplaces first. Optimize your product listings: use clear photos on a white background, write detailed descriptions (ingredients, benefits, size), and set a competitive price. Offer promotions: free delivery for orders above KES 2,000. Respond to customer queries within 24 hours. Use a simple accounting app like Wave or QuickBooks to track online sales. Reinvest 20% of online profits into ads (Facebook or Instagram ads) to grow. Always comply with local regulations for cosmetics sales.

quiz.q: What is the recommended wholesale price for a lip balm that retails at KES 300?
quiz.explanation: Wholesale price should be 60% of retail price, so 60% of 300 is 180.

quiz.q: When approaching a local shop, what should you bring?
options: B) Free samples of each product
quiz.explanation: Bringing free samples allows the owner to try the product before committing.

quiz.q: What is a consignment arrangement?
options: A) The shop pays upfront for all stock
B) You leave stock and the shop pays after selling
C) The shop keeps all profits
D) You pay the shop to display your products
quiz.explanation: In consignment, the shop pays you only after the products are sold.

quiz.q: How often should you visit shops that take your products on consignment?
quiz.explanation: Weekly visits help check stock, collect payments, and maintain relationships.

quiz.q: What discount might you offer a shop that sells more than 50% of stock in one month?
quiz.explanation: A 5% discount on the next order is a common incentive for good performance.

quiz.q: For shipping lip balms, what is the first step in packaging?
options: A) Place in a cardboard box
B) Wrap each tube in bubble wrap or newspaper
C) Seal in a plastic bag
quiz.explanation: Individual wrapping protects the product from damage during transit.

quiz.q: What type of container is recommended for body butters during shipping?
options: B) Plastic jar with screw lid
quiz.explanation: A strong plastic jar with a screw lid prevents leakage and breakage.

quiz.q: Why should you seal hair oil bottles in a plastic bag before packing?
options: C) To make them look nice
quiz.explanation: Plastic bags contain any leaks and protect other items in the package.

quiz.q: What is a good way to fill empty spaces in a shipping box?
options: B) Shredded paper or old newspaper
quiz.explanation: Shredded paper or newspaper cushions the products and prevents movement.

quiz.q: Approximately how much does a bus company in Kenya charge to ship a small box up to 5 kg?
quiz.explanation: Local bus parcel services typically charge KES 200-500 for small boxes.

quiz.q: What should you do before using a packaging method for shipping?
options: A) Test it by dropping from waist height
quiz.explanation: A drop test simulates rough handling and ensures the packaging is adequate.

quiz.q: What is the typical cost of a 5 km boda boda delivery in Kenya?
quiz.explanation: Boda boda riders typically charge KES 150-250 for short distances within a town.

quiz.q: Which app can be used to book a boda boda in Uganda?
quiz.explanation: SafeBoda is a popular ride-hailing app for boda bodas in Uganda.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of using local courier agent networks like Pickup Mtaani?
quiz.explanation: Agent networks are cheaper because they consolidate parcels and use pickup points.

quiz.q: What should you always get as proof of delivery?
options: A) A photo or signed slip
quiz.explanation: A photo or signed slip provides evidence that the parcel was delivered.

quiz.q: What is the recommended reorder level for fast-moving items like lip balms?
quiz.explanation: For fast movers, reorder when stock drops to 20 units to avoid stockouts.

quiz.q: How often should you physically count your stock?
quiz.explanation: Weekly counts help catch discrepancies early and keep records accurate.

quiz.q: What does FIFO stand for in inventory management?
quiz.explanation: FIFO means selling older stock first to maintain freshness.

quiz.q: Where should you store your cosmetic products?
options: B) In a cool, dark place
quiz.explanation: Cool, dark storage prevents spoilage and maintains product quality.

quiz.q: What is the typical shelf life of body butters?
quiz.explanation: Body butters typically have a shelf life of about 6 months due to oils.

quiz.q: What should you do if a customer complains about a product?
options: C) Listen, apologize, and solve the problem
quiz.explanation: Good customer service involves listening, apologizing, and resolving the issue quickly.

quiz.q: What is the recommended return window for unopened products?
quiz.explanation: A 7-day return policy is common and reasonable for unopened products.

quiz.q: What should you do if a product has a quality issue like rancid smell?
options: B) Offer a replacement or refund
C) Sell it at a discount
quiz.explanation: Quality issues warrant a replacement or refund to maintain trust.

quiz.q: Why keep a returns log?
options: B) To analyze and fix root causes
quiz.explanation: A returns log helps identify patterns and improve production or packaging.

quiz.q: What is a fast way to issue refunds?
quiz.explanation: Mobile money is instant and widely used in Africa for refunds.

quiz.q: Which social media platform is good for showing how products are made?
quiz.explanation: TikTok is ideal for short, engaging videos showing production processes.

quiz.q: What is a popular online marketplace in Nigeria?
quiz.explanation: Jumia is a major e-commerce platform in Nigeria and other African countries.

quiz.q: What commission do online marketplaces typically charge?
quiz.explanation: Most marketplaces charge a commission of 10-15% on each sale.

quiz.q: What should you include in an online product listing?
options: B) Clear photos and detailed description
quiz.explanation: Clear photos and detailed descriptions help customers make informed decisions.

quiz.q: What percentage of online profits should be reinvested into ads?
quiz.explanation: Reinvesting 20% into ads helps grow online sales sustainably.
